# Subscriptions and promotions

Status: non-Arete implementation completed locally; physical-device checks recorded below. Production commerce activation and transaction validation remain outstanding. Updated September 9, 2026. The implemented structure is Free plus two paid tiers, Plus and Max, each with monthly and annual billing. Advanced Arete remains deferred and is not advertised as delivered. Production prices and offers require App Store Connect configuration.

This document owns the subscription comparison, proposed tier boundaries, and in-app conversion campaigns for Paths. It separates repository behavior from proposed work. No products, prices, offers, or App Store territories were changed during this audit. App Store Connect configuration and production purchase behavior were not inspected.

## Implementation record — September 9, 2026

The user authorized implementing the discussed subscription and self-promotion work, explicitly excluding Arete refinement. The tables and experiments below preserve the decision history; proposed prices, discounts and future AI capabilities are not live product claims.

### Implemented access

| Capability | Free | Plus | Max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Existing calendar, practice, proof, reminders, history, social features and earned progress | Preserved | Included | Included |
| Feature suggestions | Included | Included | Included |
| Fits, expressions, comparison and undo | Preserved; newly applied assets require access | Included | Included |
| Frozen avatar asset catalog | 162 catalog assets | 209 catalog assets | All 230 catalog assets |
| Frozen static calendar catalog | 20 backgrounds | 48 backgrounds | All 77 backgrounds |
| Practice insights | Existing history remains free | 7/30/90-day comparisons by pattern and a seven-day summary | Included |
| Saved practice plans | Read and delete existing plans | Save current schedules and reopen each available pattern in the existing scheduling editor | Included |
| Arete | Existing assistance unchanged | Existing assistance unchanged | Existing assistance unchanged; advanced Arete deferred |

Avatar counts describe catalog files, not the number of compatible outfits or choices available to one body/archetype. Identity features and a complete starter appearance for every body/archetype remain free. Earned Story objects remain under their existing earned-unlock rules and are excluded from paid asset counts.

`SubscriptionAssetCatalog.swift` freezes assignments by domain and asset basename. Reordering or adding assets cannot silently change an existing assignment. Every new selectable asset needs an explicit entry and catalog coverage test. Unassigned assets conservatively require Max until assigned. Max does not override compatibility or earned Story conditions.

Saved plans are account-scoped local device records. They preserve the scheduled pattern, weekdays, times, color and reminder selection. Reuse requires an available template and opens the ordinary editor for conflict checking and explicit scheduling; it never bulk-overwrites active schedules or completion history. Already scheduled or unavailable patterns are labeled. A confirmation precedes replacing an unsaved scheduling draft. Cross-device plan synchronization is not included.

Insights count loaded completion records, exclude skipped and future dates, and compare the current period (including partial today) with the preceding equally sized period. They include loaded archived patterns. They do not imply a completion rate or a comparison adjusted for changes in schedule frequency.

### Compatibility and expiry

| Verified existing product | New access |
| --- | --- |
| Bronze or Silver, monthly or annual | Plus |
| Gold, Diamond or Ruby, monthly or annual | Max |
| Plus / Max | Corresponding new tier |
| Unrecognized product or no verified current entitlement | Free |

Only exact recognized product identifiers grant access. Legacy configurable identifiers remain recognized; new sales use only the four Plus/Max identifiers. Existing `subscription_tier` profile metadata remains `silver`/`gold`/`none` for old readers; `subscription_plan` records `plus`/`max`/`none`. UI authorization uses verified StoreKit state, not editable profile metadata. Profile sync compares the original JSON before writing and retries conflicts so another profile change is not overwritten. Auth-preview runs bypass account writes.

The transaction listener handles verified updates outside the purchase screen. Current entitlements exclude revoked and superseded transactions and retain Apple's subscribed/grace-period entitlement semantics. Billing recovery takes priority over acquisition messaging. Account-sync failures do not remove locally verified benefits.

Expiry no longer normalizes the worn avatar to free replacements. Saved appearances and Fits stay intact. Newly applying an asset, Fit or outfit checks the current tier; contextual explanations preserve the attempted selection. After checkout, users return to the originating screen and explicitly apply their preserved selection. No purchase auto-applies a look or destroys existing edits.

### Checkout and promotion delivery

- Free is explained alongside Plus and Max. Monthly and annual access is identical. Cards use StoreKit-localized prices only; unavailable products have disabled purchase actions. Annual savings are calculated against twelve current monthly payments in the same currency, rounded down.
- Apple's `SubscriptionStoreView` presents purchase confirmation, eligible offers and renewal terms. The app provides restore purchases, manage/cancel, account-sync retry, and configured privacy/terms links. Checkout remains unavailable if legal URLs are missing. Product-load failure never substitutes a made-up price.
- Contextual prompts appear in avatar selection, Fits/Explore and calendar backgrounds, and for the new premium tools. They recommend the lowest sufficient tier. They offer a dismissal and keep the original task available.
- 2026-10-08: the promotion banner is mounted on Profile again, as a full-width tile under the avatar card (it was lost in the 2026-09-28 Profile rewrite). Until that fix its tasks never started (an empty `Group` never runs `.task`), so no promotion had shown on any surface; the calendar placement now resolves only when a seasonal campaign is configured. The banner also resolves only while checkout can sell (`PATHS_PRIVACY_POLICY_URL` and `PATHS_TERMS_URL` both configured), so in real builds it first appears when order-of-work item 8 unblocks checkout; to show it earlier, remove `Self.checkoutIsAvailable,` from the first guard in `SubscriptionPromotions.resolve()`. It also stays hidden while a level-up or Arete requirement celebration is on screen (`.progressLevelReached`, `.areteRequirementCompleted`).
- Proactive self-promotion is limited to Profile and the calendar overview. Regular Plus promotion appears in Profile. Configured verified discounts may appear in Profile; calendar acquisition is seasonal only. No third-party ad SDK, marketing push, practice interruption or earned-status upsell is added.
- Proactive activation conservatively requires a signed-in, onboarded account, two completed days and 48 hours since this device first records the account's promotion history. The 48-hour clock does not backdate to an unknown account creation time. Explicit plan access remains available immediately.
- One proactive impression per app session and at most two per seven days, shared across placements and campaign types. Campaign dismissal suppresses it for fourteen days. A second dismissal within thirty days suppresses all proactive acquisition for thirty days from that dismissal. Purchase, billing recovery, pending checkout, uncertain billing status and account-sync errors suppress acquisition. Storefront changes and campaign expiry clear displayed campaigns.
- Eligible introductory offers are indicated in plan comparison and fully disclosed by Apple at checkout. A returning-subscriber campaign additionally requires verified win-back eligibility and at least thirty days since expiry. Campaign claims never infer eligibility from merely having an offer configured.

### Verification

On September 9, 2026, the physical iPhone 16 Plus completed 26 passing tests across subscription policy, catalog coverage, savings calculations, promotion caps, insights, saved-plan snapshots, avatar artwork and Fits. The app and test targets compile successfully for the physical-device destination. Six subscription/practice screenshots cover Plus, Max, unavailable products, large text, contextual upgrade explanation, free insights and a paid insights fixture. Images are under `Methods_Images/subscriptions-plus-max/`.

Two automated StoreKit transaction tests could not run: the local test service rejected both generated and bundled configuration with `SKInternalErrorDomain Code=3`, returning no fixture products. They are explicitly skipped when the local fixture cannot be activated; that is not evidence that purchase, refund, renewal or restore scenarios passed. The retained test fixture uses synthetic prices only. App Store sandbox verification of real products, offers, pending approval, billing recovery and renewal remains a launch requirement. No simulator or production purchase was used.

Device results: `/tmp/paths-subscriptions-tests-final.xcresult` (24 passed, 2 skipped) and `/tmp/paths-subscriptions-practice-tests.xcresult` (2 passed). Whitespace checks passed for modified tracked subscription, profile, avatar and calendar sources. The existing avatar display work remains intact. The final device build passed and was installed. Auth-preview and forced-signup flags were explicitly cleared; the launch log confirmed `Showing CoreFlow (main app/calendar)`, followed by a normal launch without test arguments.

### Production configuration still required

These are external launch prerequisites, not capabilities this code can create in App Store Connect:

1. Configure Plus monthly/annual and Max monthly/annual in one subscription group, with Max above Plus. Set prices, availability, tax and review metadata. Preserve existing subscription products for entitlement migration; do not delete or forcibly repurchase them.
2. Supply `PATHS_SUBSCRIPTION_PLUS_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID`, `PATHS_SUBSCRIPTION_PLUS_YEARLY_PRODUCT_ID`, `PATHS_SUBSCRIPTION_MAX_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID`, and `PATHS_SUBSCRIPTION_MAX_YEARLY_PRODUCT_ID`. Defaults are `com.paths.subscription.{plus|max}.{monthly|yearly}`. Supply real `PATHS_PRIVACY_POLICY_URL` and `PATHS_TERMS_URL`.
3. Configure any introductory/win-back offers in App Store Connect before advertising them. Signed promotional offers are not enabled: they require an authenticated signing backend and a separately configured offer. No signing credential belongs in the app.
4. Optionally set `PATHS_SUBSCRIPTION_CAMPAIGNS_JSON` to an array of records with `id`, `kind` (`discounted` or `seasonal`), `title`, `productID`, optional `offerID`, ISO-8601 `startsAt`/`endsAt`, and three-letter StoreKit `countries`. An omitted `offerID` uses the product's eligible introductory offer; a supplied identifier must match an eligible win-back offer. Campaigns are empty by default. Use neutral commercial campaign titles and real, fixed windows; Christmas may be a commercial campaign, with no inference about a user's religion.
5. Keep distribution and offer availability aligned with the approved market allowlist in `SubscriptionPromotionStore.countries`: USA/CAN/MEX, EU-27, GBR/NOR/ISL/LIE/CHE. Locale and GPS are never country proxies. Unknown or unsupported storefronts receive no targeted promotion; existing entitlements are preserved.
6. Complete advanced-Arete refinement and economics before using the main planned Max differentiator in advertising. Until then, Max copy describes customization and the delivered Plus tools only. No unlimited-AI claim is made.

A production campaign should be checked in sandbox on the relevant storefront for redemption eligibility, renewal terms, expiry and return to the originating feature. Local StoreKit tests use fixture prices and do not establish production product or offer readiness. [Apple: StoreKit testing](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekittest/sktestsession).


## 1. What each subscription unlocks today

Monthly and annual billing unlock the same features. At the preimplementation audit, the hierarchy was Free → Bronze → Silver → Gold; legacy Diamond and Ruby identifiers map to Gold. Subscription names are unrelated to Bronze/Silver/Gold accomplishment badges or social medals. Paying must not imply earning those achievements.

| Capability | Free | Bronze | Silver | Gold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Avatar asset choices | First 22% by entitlement ordering | First 40% | First 60% | 100% |
| Static calendar asset backgrounds | First 22% by entitlement ordering | First 40% | First 60% | 100% |
| Basic/non-asset calendar backgrounds | Available where the option is otherwise supported | Same | Same | Same |
| Suggest New Features entry point | Locked | Locked | Available | Available |
| Fits: save, wear, rename, replace, favorite, delete | No separate subscription gate found; wearing validates every included asset | Same, with tier's assets | Same | Same |
| Undo/redo, comparison, component favorites and exploration locks | No separate subscription gate found | Same | Same | Same |
| Explore / Surprise | Only eligible, unlocked clothing/background combinations | More eligible combinations | More eligible combinations | All compatible combinations |
| Expressions | No separate subscription gate found | Same | Same | Same |
| Story decorations | Earned through 1/3/6 badges; not bought through a plan | Same | Same | Same |
| Animated calendar backgrounds | Coming soon; unavailable | Unavailable | Unavailable | Unavailable |
| Priority feature review / concierge requests | No live entitlement definition | No live entitlement definition | No live entitlement definition | No live entitlement definition |
| Calendar, pattern practice, proof methods, progress, social features | No subscription gate found in the audited entitlement call sites; normal product requirements still apply | Same | Same | Same |
| Arete | No plan-specific paid allowance found; auxiliary-provider usage policy exists separately | Same | Same | Same |
| Groups | Outside current release navigation according to the product slate; do not sell access | Same | Same | Same |

**The percentages are not a fixed named catalog.** The service rounds upward: `min(total, max(1, ceil(total × ratio)))` for a nonempty pool. For ten choices, the result is 3/4/6/10, not exactly 22/40/60/100 percent. Avatar pools depend on compatible categories/accessory groups; removal and placeholder entries are excluded. Archetype visibility and earned unlocks apply separately. “Gold unlocks everything” would therefore be inaccurate: say “all subscription-eligible static assets,” not every earned, incompatible, or unfinished feature.

The current ordering-based policy can change an asset's required tier when catalogs grow or reorder. Before launch, publish an explicit asset-ID-to-minimum-tier manifest and derive picker locks and comparison counts from it. Keep a complete, attractive free avatar for each body and archetype; do not charge merely to choose a body, skin tone, or basic facial identity. Grandfather existing access deliberately rather than allowing ordering changes to decide it.

### Current price display, not verified storefront prices

| Plan | Monthly fallback shown in code | Annual fallback shown in code |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Bronze | $9.99 | $99.99 |
| Silver | $19.99 | $199.99 |
| Gold | $39.99 | $399.99 |

The UI prefers StoreKit's localized `displayPrice`, but falls back to hardcoded dollar amounts. Annual cards hardcode “Save 17%.” These are implementation facts, not approved regional prices. Product identifiers are configurable; the release checklist still calls for final identifiers. Do not advertise these prices internationally without verified StoreKit products.

**Product hypothesis, revised after research:** current tiers have limited functional differentiation, but that does not establish that three tiers are commercially wrong. Some customers may pay more for completeness, identity, convenience, or patronage. A premium tier does not need benefits proportional to its price. Test its incremental contribution and its effect on lower-tier sales rather than assuming either that it harms conversion or that it cannot harm conversion. Section 9 records the evidence and proposed experiment.

## 2. Accepted tier direction: Free, Plus and Max

The user chose two paid tiers: **Plus and Max**, each with monthly and annual billing. There is no third paid tier in the current plan. Section 1 preserves the audit of the existing Bronze/Silver/Gold implementation; those names and prices are not the new product contract. Existing subscription mappings and access must be migrated deliberately, not changed by merely renaming cards.

**A substantially more powerful and capable Arete is the main reason to choose Max over Plus.** Complete customization and premium cosmetic collections are supporting benefits, not the principal distinction. The current Arete needs substantial refinement before it can deliver this promise.

| Capability | Free | Plus | Max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Core calendar, practice/proof, basic reminders, progress and earned badges | Included | Included | Included |
| Existing social participation, safety/reporting and account controls | Included | Included | Included |
| Existing Fits tools, expressions, comparison and undo | Included; asset eligibility applies | Included | Included |
| Static avatar/background library | Attractive starter collection | Broad paid collection | Complete subscription-eligible collection; distinctive coordinated styles |
| Existing personal history and access to records | Included | Included | Included |
| New comparisons, trend filters and reusable planning templates | Not part of the proposed free expansion | Proposed practical premium capabilities, subject to delivery | Includes Plus |
| Arete | Preserve existing assistance while defining the future baseline | Standard assistance; exact additional capability and allowance remain to be specified | Significantly stronger reasoning and everyday conversation, deeper Paths context, longer conversations and a substantial measured usage allowance |
| User-controlled persistent memory, document help and richer planning | Exact baseline remains to be specified | Exact boundary remains to be specified | Refinement targets for the advanced Arete experience |
| Earned Story objects, badges, points and rank | Earned | Earned | Earned; never granted by payment |
| Bug reports, safety reports and ordinary product feedback | Included | Included | Included |

The tier names and advanced-Arete differentiator are accepted. Individual feature boundaries in this table are proposed, not claims of shipped access. Ordinary feature suggestions should move out of the paid gate. Preserve existing free functionality while defining the new contract; do not quietly impose new restrictions on current Arete users.

### Arete refinement is required work for Max

Product ambition: **a personal AI connected to the user's life in Paths**, capable enough that users may choose it for regular LLM conversation. General conversation should be supported. Planning, learning, reflection and daily decisions grounded in Paths are the initial areas of strength. Replacing every general-purpose AI subscription is a long-term ambition, not a launch claim.

Carry the following work into [Arete Architecture](Arete-Architecture.md). Its existing specification is an input, not evidence that these capabilities have shipped.

- [ ] Audit current Arete behavior against the Max ambition and identify the concrete gaps before implementation.
- [ ] Improve response quality: reasoning, instruction following, useful follow-up questions, general conversation, writing and learning assistance. A stronger model name alone is not proof of a better experience.
- [ ] Make Paths knowledge and user context accurate and current. Distinguish retrieved facts from guesses, handle missing or stale data, and avoid repeatedly asking for information already available.
- [ ] Refine long conversations and continuity. Define user-controlled memory with inspect, correct, forget and disable controls, and enforce account isolation.
- [ ] Define and validate document assistance and source-backed research where needed. Decide the launch scope for files, search and images explicitly rather than promising full parity with other chat products.
- [ ] Refine planning and authorized in-app actions: show meaningful proposed changes, apply them reliably, and handle cancellation, conflicts and failures without duplicate actions or lost user work.
- [ ] Improve chat usability and reliability: responsive streaming, interruption, retry, conversation history and clear failure recovery.
- [ ] Define observable differences between standard Arete in Plus and advanced Arete in Max. Specify model/tool access, context limits and usage allowances without reducing the distinction to vague “smarter AI” copy.
- [ ] Measure inference, search, file-processing and memory costs under ordinary and heavy daily use. Choose pricing, allowances and fallback behavior from those measurements. Show usage/reset information; do not promise unlimited premium reasoning. The earlier draft's 20 planning sessions per month is superseded and is not the Max allowance.
- [ ] Build a representative evaluation set covering Paths guidance, planning, reflection, general chat, long conversations, documents and failure recovery. Compare current, Plus-target and Max-target behavior against the same tasks. Set quality, latency, reliability and cost acceptance thresholds before launch evaluation.
- [ ] Validate the implemented experience on the physical iPhone, including existing-user access and subscription transitions. Do not sell unfinished advanced capabilities as current benefits.

**Readiness condition:** Max's advanced-Arete promise is launch-ready only when the defined capabilities are implemented, the agreed evaluation thresholds pass, and measured usage economics support the displayed allowance. If this work is incomplete, delay that promise or Max's launch rather than advertising the refinement backlog as delivered.

### Other tier boundaries and migration

Keep animated backgrounds out of sales copy until delivered. Concierge service is excluded without an actual staffed service and defined scope. Do not gate basic proof, badge requirements, safety tools, restoration, cancellation or retrieval of existing personal records. Optional supporter recognition must remain visibly separate from earned achievements.

After cancellation, retain benefits through the verified paid-through date. On expiry, keep saved Fits, conversations and personal data; explain unavailable paid operations without deleting or silently rewriting content. Recommended cosmetic policy: retain the last worn appearance, but require the necessary tier to newly apply a paid asset or Fit. Reconcile this explicitly with existing downgrade normalization before implementation. Handle grace periods, refunds, revocations, upgrades and billing recovery through verified entitlements. Document how existing Bronze/Silver/Gold and legacy subscribers map to Plus/Max before changing products or gates.

## 3. Banner types and exact placement proposals

A banner promotes a useful next action. It opens the relevant plan/offer with the originating feature preserved; after successful purchase, return to that feature. It never purchases directly from a misleading one-tap label.

| Placement | Trigger and timing | Banner / message | Destination |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Avatar customizer | User taps a locked asset; beneath the portrait, above asset controls | Regular: “This look is included in Plus.” Show the selected asset and its actual minimum tier. | Comparison focused on the lowest tier that unlocks it |
| Calendar background picker | User taps a locked static background; inline beneath preview | Regular: “Make this setting yours with Plus.” Substitute actual tier. | Relevant plan; preserve current selection |
| Fits / Explore | User explicitly tries an outfit containing locked assets | Regular: explain which pieces are locked; do not discard the saved Fit | Lowest tier covering every locked piece |
| Profile | Compact card below account/plan summary; only after activation | Regular: one concrete benefit, such as “Explore more avatar styles.” | Plan comparison |
| Progress | After a user opens a future premium comparison control | Regular: “Compare patterns over time with Plus.” Only after the feature ships. | Comparison preview and plan |
| Manage subscription | Above plan comparison, when an eligible offer is resolved | Discounted: exact introductory or returning-subscriber terms | Matching StoreKit product and offer |
| Calendar overview | Below the day's summary, after the first completed activity and only outside active practice | Seasonal: one dismissible card for a verified regional campaign | Matching offer and full terms |
| Returning-user Profile visit | Subscription expired at least 30 days ago; after user resumes an ordinary task | Discounted: welcome-back message only if redemption eligibility is verified | Eligible win-back/promotional offer |

“After activation” initially means onboarding complete, two completed activities on separate days, and at least 48 hours since account creation. These are experiment defaults, not required tasks to access a purchased subscription. User-initiated plan access and locked-feature explanations remain available immediately.

**Do not place acquisition banners** inside timers, workouts, camera/microphone capture, evidence submission, alarm dismissal, permission dialogs, authentication, peer-review composition, or cancellation/restore/error flows. Avoid inserting them into friends' posts or accomplishment celebrations. Never cover the avatar or the action the user came to perform.

### Presentation and frequency

- One in-flow banner at a time; no modal on launch, sticky obstruction, autoplay, flashing countdown, or fake scarcity.
- One proactive impression per session, at most two in seven days across all campaign types. A dismissal suppresses that campaign for 14 days or until it ends, whichever comes first. Two proactive dismissals suppress all proactive acquisition banners for 30 days.
- Explicit locked-item taps may show a small contextual explanation despite the proactive cap; they must not create a separate discount popup on every tap.
- Hide acquisition banners after purchase. Existing subscribers see only relevant higher-tier benefits or an eligible billing-period offer. Max annual subscribers see no upgrade acquisition banners.
- Billing retry, pending purchase, entitlement uncertainty, and restore in progress suppress acquisition campaigns. Recovery messaging takes priority.
- Banner priority: necessary service message, then requested feature explanation, then eligible seasonal offer, then eligible nonseasonal discount, then regular promotion. Never stack offers.
- Use a readable title, one benefit, a clear action and dismiss control. Support Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, reduced motion, and adequate contrast. A “Not now” action keeps the current task intact.

## 4. Regular, discounted, and seasonal pricing

“Seasonal” describes campaign timing and artwork; it is not a separate StoreKit offer type. The same feature access applies regardless of whether a subscriber used a promotion.

| Campaign | Initial proposal, subject to economics and StoreKit configuration | Suitable audience |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular | Actual monthly/annual price; annual savings compared with 12 current monthly payments | Anyone able to buy the displayed product |
| First subscription discount | Candidate 20% off the first annual term, then the standard annual renewal price | StoreKit-confirmed introductory eligibility |
| Returning subscriber discount | Candidate 25% off one billing period, then standard renewal | Eligible lapsed subscribers; start testing after 30 days lapsed |
| Seasonal discount | Candidate up to 25% off the first annual term; one defined campaign window | Only the audience eligible for the underlying configured offer |

The percentages above are test proposals, not currently redeemable promises. Match available local price points and calculate the actual percentage, rather than claiming an exact discount the storefront cannot deliver. Do not introduce a free trial and a paid discount simultaneously in the first experiment.

Use an introductory offer for eligible first-time customers; eligibility is once per subscription group, not once per app account or tier. Determine it before showing an introductory claim. [Apple: introductory offers](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/set-up-introductory-offers-for-auto-renewable-subscriptions/).

Promotional offers can serve existing or previously subscribed customers, including qualifying upgrades. They require configured offers and secure signing; do not ship signing credentials in the app. They are not a substitute for new-customer introductory eligibility. [Apple: promotional offers](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/set-up-promotional-offers-for-auto-renewable-subscriptions).

For churned customers, use configured win-back eligibility; the available-offer list alone does not establish eligibility. Implement support only on supported OS versions, with a regular-price fallback. [Apple: supporting win-back offers](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/supporting-win-back-offers-in-your-app), [Apple: offer eligibility](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/product/subscriptioninfo/winbackoffers).

Offer codes are a separate option for deliberately distributed campaigns with configured customer eligibility. Do not publish a generic coupon box implying arbitrary percentage codes will work. [Apple: subscription offer codes](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/set-up-subscription-offer-codes/).

Every offer view must state the plan, amount billed now, introductory duration, renewal amount and frequency, and eligibility restrictions. For annual plans, show the full annual charge more prominently than a monthly equivalent. Include restoration, subscription management, Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. [Apple: subscription purchase experience](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/subscriptions/).

Example template, populated from verified local product data:

> **New Year, your next chapter**\
> Max: **{offer price} for your first year**. Then {regular annual price}/year, auto-renewing until canceled. Eligible new subscribers only. Offer ends {date and time zone}.\
> **View offer** · Not now

Never reset an expired countdown, invent a previous price, or advertise permanent savings for a first-term discount. If product loading or eligibility fails, show a regular non-price benefit card or no campaign; never substitute the hardcoded dollar fallback.

## 5. Country selection and seasonal calendar

Use **App Store storefront country** for product pricing, redemption availability, and commercial campaign eligibility. It is not the user's birthplace, nationality, language, physical location, or inferred religion. StoreKit provides a three-letter storefront country code. Language controls copy; an optional preference can hide seasonal promotions. [Apple: Storefront.countryCode](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/storefront/countrycode).

Working market assumption: United States, Canada and Mexico for the initial North American campaign catalog; EU-27, United Kingdom, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland for the initial European catalog. This is an explicit launch proposal, not an assertion that these exhaust either continent. Other European, Central American and Caribbean storefronts need an explicit availability/localization decision before inclusion. Maintain one approved country allowlist shared by app distribution, product availability and campaigns. Do not infer market availability from the device language or GPS. Unknown or unapproved storefront: no targeted campaign; preserve existing entitlements.

| Campaign | Proposed window | Country treatment | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| New Year / fresh start | January 1–10 | All approved storefronts with localized copy | Primary campaign; naturally relevant to Paths |
| Spring refresh | One selected week in March–April | Approved storefronts; neutral seasonal language | Optional; do not use Easter as a proxy |
| Return to routine | One local 7-day window in late August–September | Country-specific timing and copy; avoid assuming school attendance | Primary campaign |
| Black Friday / Cyber Monday | Friday through Monday of the selected year's retail weekend | US/Canada first; other storefronts only after local merchandising review | Optional pilot, not automatic Europe-wide targeting |
| Christmas / year-end | December 18–26 | Christmas wording only in explicitly reviewed locales; neutral “Year-end offer” elsewhere | Commercial framing; no inferred personal observance |
| Boxing Day | December 26–28 | Candidate Canada/UK; enable only after local review | Alternative to the Christmas campaign, not an overlapping second offer |

Start with **three campaigns per year**: New Year, return to routine, and one year-end campaign. The other rows are alternatives, not six mandatory sales. Store concrete start/end timestamps per campaign and eligible storefront, with an explicit time zone; do not let travel or a changed device clock extend offers. Local dates and translations need verification for the chosen year before activation. This is a merchandising calendar, not a legal holiday calendar.

No devotional, religion-specific, bereavement, conflict, or disaster-based campaigns. Christmas is the named commercial exception requested for this product; do not extrapolate that exception to every religious holiday. Mexico and individual European countries deserve their own copy review, not a translation of US Thanksgiving messaging.

## 6. Apple's position and review requirements

**Christmas naming:** no blanket prohibition was found in the reviewed guidelines. Sections 1.1.1 and 1.1.5 address discriminatory/offensive religious material and inflammatory religious commentary. A respectful commercial Christmas offer therefore appears compatible; this is an interpretation, not pre-approval. [Apple: App Review Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/).

Subscriptions must provide ongoing value, describe what the customer receives, and support seamless tier changes. Misleading subscription marketing is prohibited. Configure the four target Plus/Max monthly/annual products in one appropriate subscription group with correct levels. Paid access must not depend on completing invitations or other marketing tasks. [Apple: guidelines 3.1.2(a–c)](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#subscriptions).

Use StoreKit purchases for this proposal. Regional external-payment programs are a separate scope, not a shortcut for campaign implementation. Marketing push requires explicit in-app opt-in and opt-out under 4.5.4; ordinary reminder permission is not marketing consent. Launch banners in-app only. [Apple: guidelines 4.5.4](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/#apple-sites-and-services).

Apple review does not settle country-specific consumer, reference-price, renewal or marketing obligations. Those remain a prelaunch review per selected jurisdiction; this document does not claim a uniform North American/European discount law.

## 7. Implementation sequence and acceptance checks

1. Approve the market allowlist, tier table, free baseline, expiry behavior and price/value hypothesis. Define Plus/Max boundaries and complete the advanced-Arete readiness work in Section 2.
2. Replace percentage-only entitlements with stable asset assignments; keep a machine-readable feature catalog shared by locks and paywall copy. Document existing-user protection. Verify server-side authorization for any paid server service; a UI gate or editable profile field is not proof of entitlement.
3. Fix commerce readiness: actual product IDs, StoreKit-only prices, calculated annual savings, renewal/legal copy, management/restore, and entitlement lifecycle. The current purchase path calls `product.purchase()` without an offer selection; promotion delivery is new work.
4. Add regular contextual banners first, preserving the attempted selection and recommending the lowest sufficient tier. Instrument exposure, click, paywall view, verified purchase, dismissal and return to task.
5. Add one verified introductory offer. Then add country-aware seasonal merchandising. Win-back offers come after lifecycle and eligibility validation.
6. Test on the physical iPhone using StoreKit/sandbox accounts: Free plus Plus/Max × monthly/annual, alongside legacy Bronze/Silver/Gold migration cases; new/current/lapsed/ineligible; product-load failure; storefront changes; offer expiry; pending/canceled purchases; refund/revocation/grace/restore; downgrade with saved Fits; dismissal caps across screens; large text; successful return to the originating feature. No production purchases are implied by this plan.

Evaluate conversion alongside retained paid subscribers, net revenue after discounts/refunds/store fees, cancellation, dismissal, and completion of the original task. Use an account-level holdout to check whether banners add purchases rather than merely discounting people who would have subscribed anyway. Do not declare a winning campaign from click-through alone. Avoid recording reflection text, religion, contacts, or proof media in campaign analytics.

## 9. Spending segments and premium-tier research

Research date: September 9, 2026. This section revises the earlier conversational recommendation to launch only one paid tier. That recommendation was too categorical. A useful premium option is a valid commercial hypothesis even when its incremental functionality is modest. Neither a universal four-personality taxonomy nor a three-tier optimum is established by the evidence below.

### What the public evidence establishes

Apple's published 2024 US ecosystem study separates physical goods/services, advertising, and digital goods/services; it is not a consumer-level spending segmentation. The headline $406 billion must not be treated as iOS subscription spending. No Apple-published market shares for the four proposed customer types were identified in this review. [Apple's official release](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/05/app-store-in-the-us-facilitated-406-billion-usd-in-developer-billings-and-sales-in-2024/).

Duolingo's 2025 Form 10-K reports approximately 9% paid subscriber penetration among monthly active users, and describes Super and Max. This is first-party evidence of a large free audience alongside multiple paid offerings. It covers Duolingo across platforms, not iOS alone, and neither proves permanent nonpayment nor identifies why Max customers choose it. [Duolingo 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1562088/000162828026012494/duol-20251231.htm).

RevenueCat's 2026 report covers over 115,000 apps. It reports 23% of freemium conversions occurring six or more weeks after download, and about 20% one-year reactivation among churned monthly subscribers. These vendor-cohort figures are not an Apple census or iOS-only results. They support distinguishing current nonpayment from permanent refusal, and episodic purchasing from randomness. [RevenueCat 2026](https://www.revenuecat.com/state-of-subscription-apps).

A 2021 study pooled self-reported data from 7,767 loot-box purchasers: the highest-spending 5% accounted for approximately half of spending in the sample. Spending correlated with problem-gambling scores, but not significantly with earnings. This supports concentration within that setting, not an estimate for ordinary app subscriptions or proof that every high spender is compulsive. [Close and colleagues, author repository](https://pearl.plymouth.ac.uk/pms-research/529/).

A survey of 519 in-game purchasers identified six motivational dimensions, including social, economic, competitive, content-unlocking and friction-removal motives. Customers can have multiple motives; a transaction total cannot distinguish them. This is gaming research, not a validation of a general iOS personality model. [Hamari and colleagues, 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0747563216307865).

### Operational interpretation of the four proposed types

| Proposed label | Useful observation | What must not be inferred | Paths response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Freeloaders / never-spenders | No observed purchase within a defined time window | Permanent refusal across every app, or no indirect contribution | Measure activated nonpayers separately from abandoned installs; keep acquisition spending proportionate to conversion likelihood |
| Enigmas / sporadic spenders | Irregular purchases, lapses and returns | Absence of a reason or inability to predict probabilities | Record campaign exposure, tenure, billing period and product use; test return-at-need offers |
| Pragmatists / functional spenders | Payment associated with a concrete task or benefit | Perfectly rational, immediately canceling, or necessarily low spending | Offer a strong core paid package and measure actual renewal drivers |
| Whales / high spenders | High net spend or premium-plan adoption | Wealth, compulsivity, status motivation, or predictable loyalty | Offer a real premium package; ask optional purchase-reason questions and track retention |

Use two independent dimensions: spending behavior and purchasing motivation. A functional buyer can be a heavy spender; a status buyer can buy once; a heavy spender can lapse. A customer can also be a nonpayer in Paths and a large payer elsewhere. Impulse purchases are not automatically compulsive purchases. Compulsion is a separate loss-of-control/harm question, not a tier-selection attribute or target segment.

For analytics, use explicit states such as observed nonpayer, first-time payer, retained payer, lapsed payer and reactivated payer, plus net-spend and tenure measures. Compare annual/monthly subscribers over comparable periods and account for discounts/refunds. Add motivations only when supported by an optional survey or behavioral experiment. Do not assign inferred psychological diagnoses.

### The expensive-tier hypothesis

Choice research supports a compromise effect: an intermediate option can gain share when the comparison set changes. That gives a plausible additional reason for a premium tier even if relatively few customers buy it. It does not establish an increase in total paid conversion. [Simonson, 1989](https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/publications/choice-based-reasons-case-attraction-compromise-effects).

Conversely, a meta-analysis of 50 experiments with 5,036 participants found a near-zero average choice-overload effect with substantial variation. Neither “more choices always hurt” nor “an extra tier cannot hurt” is justified. These are general consumer-choice studies, not Paths paywall experiments. [Scheibehenne and colleagues, 2010](https://bear.warrington.ufl.edu/brenner/mar7588/Papers/scheibehenne-jcr2010.pdf).

For Paths, the accepted premium package is Max, led by a substantially more capable Arete. Complete subscription-eligible customization, distinctive collections and optional supporter recognition are secondary benefits; recognition remains separate from earned badges. Buying every eligible option or supporting the product can be a legitimate benefit. Do not claim that this audience requires, or exhibits, compulsive spending. A fixed subscription also caps individual expenditure, unlike repeatable game microtransactions; gaming whale concentration is not a revenue forecast for Paths.

The earlier tier-count experiment remains an optional validation method, not an unresolved product decision: (A) Free plus Plus versus (B) the identical Plus offer with Max added. Keep core benefits, price, billing periods and eligibility constant. No third paid tier is planned; reconsidering one would require a new product decision. Randomize eligible new accounts persistently; protect existing subscribers. Measure net contribution per exposed account through comparable 90-day windows, then renewals; include refunds, store fees and marginal service costs. Also track core conversion, total paid conversion, tier mix, cancellations and comprehension. Predefine a sample-size target and acceptable core-conversion loss; low traffic can leave the result inconclusive. Premium purchases alone do not prove that adding the tier helped.

Illustrative arithmetic only: 100 people at $10 yield $1,000. If 90 choose $10 and 10 choose $30, revenue is $1,200. If the additional tier instead leaves 60 at $10 and 10 at $30, revenue is $900. Prices and counts are invented; costs and renewals are excluded. The commercial question is the net change across the whole choice set, not whether anyone buys the expensive option.

## 10. Accepted advertising policy

The user accepted self-promotion only at launch: occasional dismissible Paths upgrade banners for free users, sparse relevant upgrade offers for subscribers, and no third-party advertising. Audience size alone does not automatically activate ads. A future explicitly labeled contextual sponsorship in optional discovery content would require a separate revenue/retention decision. It is not part of the current plan. No ads inside practice, reflections, proof capture or progress celebrations; no watching ads to earn points or badges.
